provenance.title: Quantitative Universal Approximation for Noisy Quantum Neural Networks
affiliations: School of Computer Science, University of St. Gallen
Department of Mathematics, Imperial College London
Department of Computing, Imperial College London
provenance.abstract: We prove a quantitative universal approximation theorem for noisy quantum neural networks (QNNs), with explicit non-asymptotic error bounds in terms of circuit width, depth, qubit count, and hardware noise parameters. Motivated by quantitative finance, we extend existing noiseless bounds to expectation functions and derive sharp constants for exponential Levy models, covering Black-Scholes European Put options, then specialise to depolarising noise calibrated to real hardware.
key_claims: Extends the noiseless universal approximation theorem of Gonon & Jacquier to expectation functions f(x)=E[Phi(x+L)], with explicit constants for exponential Levy models including Black-Scholes
Proves a fidelity-based universal approximation bound for QNNs under arbitrary CPTP noise channels (Theorem 3.6)

Derives a sharp, hardware-calibrated bound under depolarising noise with readout error, decomposing error into statistical, systematic, offset and readout terms, and shows a 2-parameter affine post-processing layer exactly cancels the depolarising bias (Theorem 3.15)

Validates the bounds experimentally by training Black-Scholes Put pricing QNNs and executing them on the IBM ibm_fez Heron r2 processor, with empirical MAE inside the analytical envelope on 10/10 test points

modules.name: state_preparation_V
modules.output_shape: equal superposition over n-2 control qubits, target qubits remain |00>
modules.notes: V is stated to be noiseless in Remark 3.5 since it consists only of Hadamard gates; noise is only injected via Psi_V/Psi_U channels around it in the general noisy formalism.

modules.name: parameterized_unitary_U
modules.operation_type: Block-diagonal parameterized unitary, decomposed via Uniformly Controlled Rotations (UCRz on qubit 0 conjugated by Hadamards, UCRy on qubit 1)
modules.output_shape: n-qubit state rho2 encoding a Fourier-like sum of n accuracy-block terms

parameters.decomposition: Uniformly Controlled Rotations (Moettoenen et al.), reduces naive O(n*n) two-qubit gate count by a factor of ~15

modules.notes: Exact gate-level circuit for the UCR decomposition is delegated to reference [23] (Moettoenen et al. 2004) and not reproduced verbatim in this paper.

modules.name: measurement
modules.operation_type: Computational basis measurement with outcome grouping modulo 4
modules.output_shape: 4 aggregated probabilities P0,P1,P2,P3 over the two target qubits

parameters.grouping_rule: outcome o = 4k+m contributes to P_m only if k < n (states with k>=n are power-of-two padding artefacts)

differences.use_case: Black-Scholes Put pricing, hardware execution on ibm_fez

optimizer.name: Three methods compared: (A) L-BFGS-B (simultaneous), (B) two-stage (fix gamma, optimise a,b, then refine gamma), (C) Adam

datasets.name: Synthetic 1D Gaussian density, x in [-4,4], 100 uniformly spaced points, sigma in {0.5,1.0,2.0}

Black-Scholes European Put pricing map: S in [0.8,1.2], K in [0.9,1.1], T in [0.5,1.0], r in [0.02,0.05], sigma in [0.1,0.3], normalised to [0,1]^5; evaluated on a 40x40 grid over (K, sigma*sqrt(T)) in [85,115]x[0.05,0.35] at fixed S0=100, r=0.03

evaluation_protocol.compute: IBM ibm_fez (Heron r2, 156 qubits) via Qiskit Runtime SamplerV2 primitive; qiskit-aer simulators for noiseless/noisy validation

implementation_assumptions.assumption: Adam optimizer (Method C) uses standard default hyperparameters (learning rate ~1e-3, beta1=0.9, beta2=0.999)
implementation_assumptions.basis: literature default; paper does not specify

implementation_assumptions.assumption: Training runs until convergence (no fixed iteration/epoch budget stated for any of Methods A/B/C)
implementation_assumptions.basis: common practice for small-scale classical optimisation of few-parameter circuits

implementation_assumptions.assumption: n0 = 0 is used throughout the main numerical experiments (so that 2^n = 4n exactly, per Remark 3.14)
implementation_assumptions.basis: inferred from Remark 3.14 being presented as the practical simplification used in the numerical section
alternatives: n0 > 0 with residual offset term retained in Corollary 3.13

implementation_assumptions.assumption: A fixed random seed is used for reproducibility of classical optimisation and simulator noise sampling
implementation_assumptions.basis: common practice; not explicitly stated in the paper
alternatives: no fixed seed / results averaged over multiple seeds

implementation_assumptions.assumption: The training-loss normalisation constant is 1/(2n) (standard MSE over n training points)
implementation_assumptions.basis: most plausible reading of the OCR/PDF-extraction-corrupted formula in Section 4.1

implementation_assumptions.assumption: Readout error probability p for ibm_fez (used in Proposition 3.20 / Eq. 4.4) is a small value obtained from live calibration, consistent with typical superconducting-hardware readout error rates (order 1e-2), since it is not listed in Appendix A Table 1
implementation_assumptions.basis: gap in the provided hardware parameter table; typical published ibm_fez readout error magnitudes
alternatives: p sourced from a separate live-calibration snapshot not reproduced in the paper

ambiguities.description: The MSE loss formula's normalisation constant is corrupted by PDF text-extraction (exponents and summation bounds rendered as stray characters), so the exact prefactor is unclear.
No learning rate, iteration count, or convergence criterion is given for L-BFGS-B, the two-stage method, or Adam.
ambiguities.primary_assumption: Defaults per optimiser, run until convergence

ambiguities.description: The readout error probability p (used in Proposition 3.20 and the hardware bound Eq. 4.4) is not listed among the ibm_fez hardware parameters in Table 1, despite being used to compute the reported total bound.
ambiguities.primary_assumption: p is taken from separate live calibration data not reproduced in the paper's table
alternatives: p omitted from the table by oversight
p assumed negligible relative to other terms

ambiguities.description: The exact gate-level sequence of the UCR decomposition of U(theta,x) is deferred to reference [23] and not reproduced in this paper.
ambiguities.primary_assumption: Standard Moettoenen et al. (2004) UCR construction (UCRz then UCRy) applied directly to the block-diagonal structure
alternatives: A custom/modified UCR gate ordering specific to this ansatz

ambiguities.description: The comprehensive noise model (amplitude damping + phase damping + depolarising) used to obtain the 0.9973 correlation figure is referenced but its precise construction beyond the Section 3.6 formulas is not fully detailed for the hardware run.
ambiguities.primary_assumption: Combination of amplitude damping (T1), phase damping (T2), and depolarising channel exactly per the Section 3.6 formulas
alternatives: Additional unmodelled noise sources such as crosstalk or leakage are also folded in
